blocks.recap_md: Nick recalls his father's advice to reserve moral judgment, though he admits his tolerance has limits.
Restless after the war, Nick leaves the Midwest for New York to learn the bond business and settles in West Egg.
Nick describes his small rented house in West Egg, across the bay from the wealthier East Egg.
Nick introduces his old classmate Tom Buchanan, a former football star, and visits Tom and Daisy's East Egg mansion.
Inside, Nick finds his cousin Daisy and her friend Jordan Baker lounging on a couch in the breezy, sunlit room.
Over drinks, the group trades light banter about Chicago gossip, the baby, and Nick's job.
Jordan casually mentions Nick's neighbor Gatsby, surprising Daisy, before the group goes in to dinner amid small tensions.
Tom passionately defends a racist pseudo-scientific book, revealing his anxious, bigoted worldview.
Amid strained dinner conversation, Jordan quietly tells Nick that Tom is involved with another woman in New York.
A phone call from Tom's mistress interrupts dinner, and the group moves outside in visible discomfort.
Daisy tells Nick, with bitter irony, that she hopes her daughter grows up to be 'a beautiful little fool.'
After the tense evening, Nick recalls that Jordan Baker, a professional golfer, was once at the center of a cheating scandal.
As Nick leaves, Tom and Daisy needle him about a rumored engagement back home, which he denies.
Driving home, Nick reflects on the Buchanans' wealth before glimpsing Gatsby alone on his lawn, reaching toward a green light across the water.

knowledge_items.statement: Nick's father advised him that whenever he feels like criticizing anyone, he should remember not everyone has had his advantages - advice Nick says has made him inclined to reserve judgment.
Nick came East, restless after the war, to learn the bond business, and rented a house in West Egg, Long Island.
Nick's house sits in West Egg, the less fashionable of the two egg-shaped peninsulas, across the bay from the more fashionable East Egg.
Tom Buchanan, Nick's old college acquaintance, had been one of the most powerful football players ever to play at New Haven.
When Nick arrives, Daisy and Jordan Baker are found reclining together on a large couch, as if just blown back in by a breeze.
When Jordan mentions that Nick must know Gatsby, Daisy reacts with surprise, asking 'What Gatsby?'
Tom enthusiastically defends a book arguing that the 'Nordic' race is losing control of civilization, revealing his anxious, bigoted worldview.
During dinner, Jordan quietly tells Nick that Tom has 'some woman in New York' - implying Tom is having an affair.
Daisy says she hopes her infant daughter will grow up to be 'a beautiful little fool,' calling that the best thing a girl can be.
Nick recalls that Jordan Baker, a professional golfer, was once at the center of an unpleasant, half-forgotten story about a tournament.
Chapter 1 ends with Nick's first glimpse of Gatsby, standing alone on his lawn and stretching his arms toward a green light across the water.

questions.prompt: According to Nick, what advice did his father give him that he has been 'turning over' in his mind ever since?
options: To always tell people exactly what he thinks of them
To remember that not everyone has had the advantages he has had
To never trust a man who has read fewer books than himself
To marry only within his own social class
questions.explanation: Nick's father told him that whenever he felt like criticizing anyone, he should remember that not all people have had the same advantages - advice Nick says left him inclined to reserve judgment.

questions.prompt: Why does Nick say he came East?
options: He inherited a house in West Egg from a relative
He wanted to escape a rumored engagement back home
Restless after the war, he decided to learn the bond business
Tom Buchanan invited him to manage the family's investments
questions.explanation: The Middle West now felt to Nick like 'the ragged edge of the universe,' so he decided to go East and learn the bond business - the rumored engagement is a different thread Tom and Daisy needle him about later.

questions.prompt: What is true about where Nick lives compared to Tom and Daisy?
options: Nick's small house in West Egg is across the bay from the more fashionable East Egg, where Tom and Daisy live
Nick lives in East Egg, in a small cottage next to Gatsby's mansion
Nick and Tom live in the same neighborhood, on opposite ends of the same street
Nick's house is directly next to Daisy's, separated only by a garden
questions.explanation: Nick describes living at West Egg, 'the - well, the less fashionable of the two,' with East Egg's white palaces visible glittering across the bay. (Gatsby's mansion is next to Nick's - but in West Egg, not East Egg.)

questions.prompt: What do we learn about Tom Buchanan's background?
options: He was a decorated war hero who served alongside Nick
He was one of the most powerful football players ever to play at New Haven
He inherited his entire fortune from Daisy's family
He worked his way up from a working-class Chicago family
questions.explanation: Nick recalls Tom as 'one of the most powerful ends that ever played football at New Haven.'

questions.prompt: How are Daisy and Jordan Baker first positioned when Nick enters the room?
options: Standing at the window, watching the sunset over the bay
Both reclining on a large couch, as if just blown back in after a flight around the house
Playing cards at a small table in the corner
Seated formally at the dining table, waiting for dinner
questions.explanation: The two women were 'buoyed up as though upon an anchored balloon' on the room's one stationary couch, their dresses still rippling as if just settled from a breeze.

questions.prompt: What happens right after Jordan tells Nick 'You must know Gatsby'?
options: Nick immediately explains that Gatsby is his old college roommate
Daisy reacts with surprised curiosity, asking 'What Gatsby?'
Tom changes the subject before Nick can answer
Daisy reveals that she and Gatsby dated years earlier
questions.explanation: Daisy 'demanded' to know 'What Gatsby?' - her surprise is a small early hint of history the reader doesn't understand yet.

questions.prompt: What does Tom's enthusiasm for the book about 'the Nordic race' reveal about his character?
options: He is well-read and genuinely curious about other cultures
He is anxious about losing racial and social dominance, and embraces pseudo-scientific bigotry
He is mocking the book's ideas to amuse Daisy
He secretly disagrees with the book but reads it to please his father
questions.explanation: Tom insists earnestly that 'we're Nordics' who 'produced all the things that go to make civilization' and that 'we've got to beat them down' - revealing an anxious, bigoted worldview, not detached curiosity.

questions.prompt: What does Jordan reveal to Nick in a hushed aside during dinner?
options: That Daisy is planning to leave Tom
That Tom has 'some woman' in New York
That Gatsby and Daisy used to be engaged
That the butler is stealing from the household
questions.explanation: Jordan says hesitantly, 'Tom's got some woman in New York' - the first direct hint of his affair.

questions.prompt: What does Daisy say she hopes for her infant daughter, and what does it reveal?
options: That she'll grow up to be a great scholar, reflecting Daisy's ambitions for her
That she'll be 'a beautiful little fool,' reflecting Daisy's disillusionment
That she'll marry a man exactly like Tom, reflecting Daisy's contentment
That she'll travel the world freely, reflecting Daisy's own restlessness
questions.explanation: Daisy says, 'I hope she'll be a fool - that's the best thing a girl can be in this world, a beautiful little fool,' a bitterly ironic line about what she's learned life expects of women.

questions.prompt: What does Nick recall about Jordan Baker once he places her face as familiar?
options: She had once been engaged to Tom before he married Daisy
There had been a critical, unpleasant story about her at a tournament
She was once a well-known silent film actress
She was Daisy's childhood governess
questions.explanation: Nick recognizes her from 'rotogravure pictures of the sporting life' and recalls hearing 'some story of her too, a critical, unpleasant story,' though he'd forgotten the details.

options: Nick falls asleep on the train back to New York
Nick sees Gatsby for the first time, standing alone and stretching his arms toward a green light across the water
Gatsby appears at Nick's door to introduce himself
Tom and Daisy argue loudly as Nick drives away
questions.explanation: Nick decides not to call out to his oddly solitary neighbor, who stretches his arms toward the dark water; Nick can make out nothing except 'a single green light' far across the bay.
